sentences.text: Smilosuchus is an extinct genus of parasuchid phytosaurs that lived during the Late Triassic in North America.
Three species of Smilosuchus are known: S. gregorii, S. adamanensis, and S. lithodendrorum, all found in the Norian-aged Chinle Formation of Arizona.
Like other phytosaurs, Smilosuchus had nostrils positioned close to the top of its head.
This predator had an extremely large skull measuring up to 155 cm long, with total body length estimates varying up to 7 meters.
Smilosuchus possessed a larger rostral crest and nasal bulge supporting its raised nostrils compared to many other phytosaurs.
Smilosuchus possessed short, broad jaws with heterodont teeth, including large anterior tusks for impaling prey and blade-like teeth at the back for slicing flesh.
Smilosuchus had short and deep squamosal processes indicating a powerful bite, and its large size suggests it hunted large prey like Placerias.
Smilosuchus lived from the Carnian to the Norian stages, approximately 237 to 205.7 million years ago.
Some studies suggest that Smilosuchus might be congeneric with Leptosuchus, proposing that the enlarged rostral crest could have evolved independently in both genera.
